speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you had a tympanoplasty; is the shooting ear pain new or did it start immediately after the surgery? Also, do you have any fever or drainage from the ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. The pain when eating suggests referred pain from the temporomandibular joint or the ear canal, while the discomfort with earrings points to a specific lesion on the tragus or cartilage. Given your history of chronic ear infections, do you notice any redness, swelling, or tenderness specifically when you touch the outer ear or the tragus?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tragal Neuralgia (Gasser's ganglion irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve).

I suspect this is neuropathic pain resulting from the previous tympanoplasty or chronic inflammation affecting the small nerves near the tragus, rather than an active infection or TMJ disorder. Since the pain is shooting and triggered by touch or eating, we do not need immediate imaging, but I want to confirm the nature of the pain before treating it with specific nerve-modulating medications. Are you experiencing a tingling or "electric shock" sensation in that area, or is it a deep, burning ache?
